_note: Learner-facing course copy, keyed by course slug. plan_courses.py owns a
course's structure — slug, classLevel, difficulty, which lessons it holds —
and this file owns the words a learner reads in the catalogue.
Three languages, always. GT_CLASS_COURSE stores BOOK_NAME (ko),
EN_BOOK_NAME and JP_BOOK_NAME and the app picks by locale, so `ja` is what
this Japanese-market track actually puts on screen and `ko` is grape's
admin label. Generating title and description from the TOC produced
English in all three slots and shipped build notation ('Core 25–36 · A1 →
A2') as the description; both are written here instead.
Length. Live cover rows average 13 characters in ko and 22 in en, with a
22-character ko maximum, so short is the house style — the generated
titles this replaced ran to 72. test_plan_courses.py holds the ceiling at
40 for en and 30 for ko/ja: the ja track prefixes (ビジネス英語,
フリートーキング) cost 6–8 characters before the theme starts, which is why
the CJK ceiling is 30 rather than the live average.
The CEFR band is the last segment of every title. It ships deliberately:
English learners in Japan read CEFR, and for free talking it is the only
thing distinguishing the accessible course from its full sibling. The two
siblings share a description — same topics, different language load — the
same way the Korean track's 중급/고급 pairs do.
